questions.text: You want a toy car sitting still to start moving. What should you do?
questions.explanation: A push or a pull makes an object start to move. Looking, talking, or waiting will not move the car.

questions.text: A ball is rolling across the floor. What can you do to make it stop?
questions.explanation: Catching the ball is a pull that stops its motion. A push forward would speed it up, not stop it.

questions.text: On a sunny day, which spot will feel the WARMEST?
questions.explanation: Sunlight warms the Earth's surface. A spot in the sunlight feels warmer than a shady or dark spot.

questions.text: It is a hot, sunny day. Which idea would keep a sandbox cooler?
options: Put an umbrella over it for shade
questions.explanation: An umbrella blocks the sunlight and makes shade, so the sandbox stays cooler. More sun would make it hotter.

questions.text: What do animals need to stay alive?
questions.explanation: Animals need food and water to live and grow. Toys and music are not things they need to survive.

questions.text: A plant on a windowsill is starting to droop. What does it most likely need?
questions.explanation: Plants need water and sunlight to stay healthy. A drooping plant usually needs water and light.

questions.text: Which kind of weather is it if the ground is wet and you see puddles?
questions.explanation: Wet ground and puddles are signs that it rained. Rain leaves water on the ground.

questions.text: In which season is it usually the coldest and most likely to snow?
questions.explanation: Winter is usually the coldest season, when snow is most likely. We can see patterns in weather across the seasons.

questions.text: A rabbit lives in a meadow. Why does it live there?
options: The meadow has grass to eat and places to hide
There is a TV to watch
It likes the color of the sky
questions.explanation: Animals live where they can find what they need. A meadow gives the rabbit food to eat and places to hide.

questions.text: You hear that a big storm is coming. What is a smart thing to do?
options: Go outside to play in it
Stay inside where it is safe
questions.explanation: When a storm warning is given, staying inside keeps you safe. Warnings help us get ready for bad weather.

questions.text: Which of these helps keep the Earth clean?
options: Putting trash in a bin and recycling
questions.explanation: Putting trash in a bin and recycling keeps the land clean and helps the Earth. Littering harms the environment.

questions.text: Which of these is a LIVING thing?
questions.explanation: A dog is living. It needs food, water, and air, and it can grow. Rocks, toy cars, and spoons are not living.

questions.text: Birds keep eating the seeds in a garden. What problem needs to be solved?
options: The birds are eating the seeds
questions.explanation: The problem is that birds are eating the seeds. Naming the problem clearly is the first step to solving it.

questions.text: You want to build a tower out of blocks. What should you do BEFORE building?
questions.explanation: Making a plan or drawing first helps you know how to build the tower. Planning comes before building.

questions.text: You build two paper airplanes and want to know which flies farther. What should you do?
options: Throw each one and see which goes farther
questions.explanation: Throwing both and comparing how far they go is a test. Testing shows which design works better.
